messages:
mike_support: FYI escalation from customer (acme-analytics) — invoices show ~30% fewer tokens than their internal audit. They run Redwood Private in a VPC with our metering agent (v1.4.2). They say audit logs contain events that never show up in billing export.

sara_sre: Can you paste the agent logs and the invoice IDs? Also whether they had any maintenance windows or agent restarts.

mike_support: Invoice IDs: INV-2025-ACME-09 and INV-2025-ACME-10. Customer reports a maintenance reboot last week (2025-06-10 03:12 UTC). Agent logs attached in their ticket — paste below the suspicious snippet they highlighted:

```
2025-06-10T03:11:58Z INFO metering-agent starting flush cycle, buffer_len=3245
2025-06-10T03:11:59Z ERROR metering.agent seq_id_wrap detected old_seq=4294967289 new_seq=3
2025-06-10T03:11:59Z WARN metering.agent drop_out_of_order seq=2 expected=4294967290
2025-06-10T03:12:00Z INFO metering.agent acked_up_to=4294967288
```

mike_support: They attached audit log entries showing user events with seq 4294967289..4294967295 and then seq 0..3 after reboot. Their auditor shows those events present, but billing export (post-processor) only persisted up to 4294967288.

alex_infra: That log looks like classic 32-bit unsigned wraparound. v1.4.2's seq counter is 32-bit and our replay/merge logic assumes monotonic increasing without wrap. When wrap happens, the deduper interprets wrapped seqs as older and drops them if ack pointer wasn't advanced. Probably explains missing tokens.

sara_sre: Has anyone seen this in prod before? We should avoid telling customer to upgrade immediately — need reconciliation path and a safe replay.

julia_pm: Customer is asking for an adjustment now — they already disputed the invoice. What's the customer-visible delta?

mike_support: They estimate ~4.2M tokens missing across the window 2025-06-09 22:00 to 2025-06-10 04:00 UTC. They have audit events for each missing request.

ingest-bot: automated: last_reconciliation_run for acme-analytics: 2025-06-10T05:00:12Z status=partial_missing_entries count_missing=8423

sara_sre: Immediate action items: (1) ask customer to provide a compact audit sample (lines with seq, ts, token_count) for the disputed range; (2) request agent debug dump from customer: `curl http://localhost:9201/debug/meter_state` and share output; (3) run our offline reconciliation tool with wrap-aware mode.

alex_infra: Recon steps we recommend internally: run ./tools/reconcile --customer acme-analytics --wrap-aware --start 2025-06-09T22:00 --end 2025-06-10T04:00 > reconc-output.log. The wrap-aware mode treats sequence numbers as modulo 2^32 and reorders by (epoch, seq) using the agent's boot timestamp.

mike_support: Customer ran the debug endpoint and pasted this snippet from `meter_state`:

```
boot_ts: 2025-06-02T11:04:19Z
last_ack: 4294967288
offline_buffer: [{seq:4294967289, tokens:120},{seq:4294967290,tokens:88},{seq:0,tokens:101},{seq:1,tokens:97}]
```

mike_support: So agent had those events in offline_buffer but last_ack stayed at 4294967288. After wrap the buffer items had seq numbers lower than last_ack numerically and were considered stale.

julia_pm: OK that confirms the root cause. What's the immediate mitigation for the customer so we can resolve the billing dispute?

alex_infra: Short-term: run the wrap-aware reconciliation tool against their offline_buffer and audit logs to generate a delta file (CSV of missing seq -> token counts). We then apply that delta to billing exports (manual adj) and mark as credit. Medium-term: release v1.4.3 patch which makes seq compare wrap-aware and persists boot_epoch in ack pointer.

sara_sre: I'll own the credit/adjustment process with billing. Alex, can you produce the delta CSV and sign off the manual adj?

alex_infra: Yes. Steps I'll run: (1) get agent dump, (2) run reconcile --wrap-aware, (3) verify checksums against customer audit sample, (4) generate reconc-delta-ACME-20250610.csv and send to billing for credit. ETA 2-3 hours.

mike_support: Customer asked for workaround they can run locally if they want quicker fix. Alex — can we provide safe CLI they can run in their VPC?

alex_infra: We can provide a read-only script to build the CSV; something like:

```bash
# read-only, does not change agent state
curl -s localhost:9201/debug/meter_state | jq -r '.offline_buffer[] | "{seq}: {tokens}"' > local-buffer.txt
./tools/reconcile --wrap-aware --buffer-file local-buffer.txt --audit-file customer-audit-sample.csv --out reconc-delta.csv
```

sara_sre: Also adding a ticket for engineering to prioritize the patch; label it P1-billing-impact. Add unit tests for wrap-around.

julia_pm: I'll communicate timeline to customer: temporary credit while we verify, patch next-week build, permanent credit if delta confirmed. Keep me posted.

mike_support: I'll reply to customer with the steps and ask for the audit sample and agent dump. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
